messages:
ashley: heads up — after the console canary this morning i can see metrics for org B showing up in org A's dashboard widgets. not full data leak but counts and some event types are mixed. :confused:
arjun: ugh. which canary? rollout id `canary-2026-03-20-09`?
ashley: yes that one. deploy-bot showed 10% traffic. i repro by switching workspaces quickly and watching the 'recent activity' panel.
kim: any query ids or request logs? could be route affinity header not sticking on the dashboard backend.
maria: checking logging now, one sample: `GET /internal/console/widgets?panel=recent&org=org-a` had `X-Org-ID: org-b` in the proxied call to insights-service.
chris: oh that's the layering bug we feared — router sets affinity for UI assets but the sidecar prefetch uses header from user session token parsing. race on rapid org switches maybe.
arjun: timeline: frontend sends org switch -> console prefetcher issues parallel fetches -> routing policy picks earlier request lane -> affinity header reused. looks like we reuse a routing context object without cloning per request.
ashley: i can reproduce with quick switch 3x. steps in case helpful: switch to org-a, open insights, switch to org-b, immediately open org-a again -> recent activity shows events from org-b for ~30s.
kim: sending a quick patch: clone RoutingContext at the start of request processing and ensure `org_id` is strictly tied to request scope. small change to `router/context.go`.
maria: telemetry-bot: alert created: "console.prefetch.org_mismatch" x5 in 2m for user ashley@redwood.com
arjun: debate: should we force strict server-side guard (reject mismatched `X-Org-ID`) or fix context cloning? rejecting can cause 500s for flaky clients. prefer defensive cloning + assertion + telemetry to catch failure modes.
chris: agree. also add a canary safety: if prefetch returns org != requested, discard results and increment metric. cheaper and safer during rollout.
ashley: +1. can we hotfix to stop data bleed in 10-15m and then ship proper test?
immediate-plan (kim): patch PR in flight: `git checkout -b fix/context-clone` -> add clone in `HandlePrefetch()` -> add unit + integration to simulate rapid org switch. will roll to canary 1% then 10% then 50%.
arjun: i'll add an internal API assertion in `router` that logs and drops mismatched responses: `if resp.org != req.org { drop(); metrics.inc("prefetch.mismatch") }`
maria: telemetry-bot: created dashboard card "prefetch.mismatch" and alert threshold at 5/min.
chris: FYI this touches routing policies/quotas too: if we drop prefetched responses we should not charge quota to the requesting org incorrectly. add a flag `billing_context` derived from request, not response.
ashley: noted. also need a small UX tweak in rollouts console: indicate "prefetch safety mode" during canary so PMs know results may be partial.
arjun: deploy-bot: canary `canary-2026-03-20-09` rollback requested by arjun at 1785554400
deploy-bot: rollback started for canary-2026-03-20-09 -> status: in-progress
maria: after rollback, i still see 1 instance showing stale results (probably buffered). will watch metrics.
chris: postmortem action items: 1) fix cloning (kim) 2) server-side assertion + drop (arjun) 3) billing guard (chris) 4) rollout UX flag (product) 5) add e2e scenario (qa)
ashley: thanks team. ping me once canary safety patch is live and alerts quiet. :thumbsup:
